conclusions.value: Token/mask/sampled-mask ownership is explicit; immutable layout/prefix metadata and separate value transport prevent later policy routing/filter mutations from changing critic input/targets. Reward replacement happens after rollout scoring; group-private prefix installation follows the complete group barrier. Value publication precedes policy filters. The original independent GAE/target lambdas, terminal reward and TETHER coefficient chronology remain.
conclusions.episode: Real canonical WireEpisode reaches an explicit single-original-trace adapter. Multi-trace episodes fail loudly before eligibility; empty or failed episodes cannot fabricate successful credit. Agent.trainable=False skips materialization. Legacy joint scoring remains server-side and partial groups remain unusable. Native tasks are selected by historical row-order RNG, serialized once per group, and reconstructed from declared TaskData/config; UUID group identity avoids aliasing semantic idx.
conclusions.packing: Metadata is optional, CPU-derived from existing lengths, and advertised only for seven custom FlashAttention families. Actor RL, value trainer and shared evaluator all thread it; CP global attention metadata and local intersected metadata remain distinct. HF/eager/SDPA/SFT and unsupported hybrid paths retain their fallback. Critic CP/VLM restrictions are not broadened.
conclusions.objectives: Safety unit stabilizes excluded-token arithmetic and diagnostics, but does not add an importance-ratio objective cap. Normalization remains component member count, not sum of weights. No hidden changes to value/model/loss config defaults were found.
conclusions.lifecycle: Atomic orchestrator progress writes and intermediate trainer counters are complementary; they do not imply transactional whole-system/sampler replay. Component exceptions interrupt orchestration rather than hanging. Conversion cache validation covers required base-model keys, shares policy/critic caches without requiring a value head, and uses a process lock plus temporary-directory publication.
